<div class="lp-block lp-content lp-content--text-alignment lp-content--text-alignment-left lp-pb-18" style="flex:1;padding-right:30px">
<h2 id="wordpress-ai-faq" class="wp-block-heading has-large-p-font-size">WordPress AI FAQ</h2>



<div class="lp-block lp-button">
<div class="wp-block-button"><a class="wp-block-button__link wp-element-button" href="https://wordpress.com/setup/ai-site-builder-onboarding?ref=ai-lp">Try the AI website builder</a></div>
</div>
</div>



<div class="lp-block lp-content" style="flex:1;margin-top:0">
<details data-event-name="faq-another-language" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">Does WordPress AI replace my creativity or writing?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">No. WordPress AI is designed to support your work, not replace it, so you stay in control of ideas, voice, and decisions. AI helps with things like tightening copy, improving clarity, formatting layouts, and optimizing for SEO when you ask.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-another-language" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">Can I use WordPress AI just as an editor?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">Yes. Many creators use the AI assistant to refine existing, human-written text — making it clearer, more concise, or better structured — without having AI generate content from scratch.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-another-language" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">Is WordPress AI only for building new sites?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">No. The AI website builder helps you create a site from scratch, and the AI assistant supports ongoing updates and improvements inside your existing site.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-another-language" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">What can the AI assistant actually help me with?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">Quite a lot. Inside your editor, you can ask it to rewrite or refine text, adjust tone, translate content, generate images from a description, edit existing photos in your Media Library, modify block styles and color palettes, create new pages, and navigate WordPress using plain language. You can also chain multiple requests together and it’ll handle them in sequence.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-another-language" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">Does the AI assistant know what’s on my site, or only general information?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">The AI assistant has context about the content you’re actively working on in the editor, but it doesn’t crawl or index your entire site by default. For deeper, site-wide awareness — like analyzing your content strategy or comparing pages — that’s what MCP agent connections are for.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-another-language" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">Can the AI assistant translate my content into other languages?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">Yes. You can ask the assistant to translate any text block into another language directly within the editor. It works across posts, pages, and other editable content on your site.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-another-language" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">What’s the difference between the AI assistant and a connected AI agent?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">The AI assistant is your in-editor helper — it responds to requests as you work and helps you create and edit content in real time. A connected AI agent (via MCP) is an external AI tool, like Claude, that you give read access to your site so it can analyze your content and provide deeper, data-driven insights. Think of the assistant as your writing partner and agents as your analysts.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-custom-domain" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">Which plans include WordPress AI?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">Build a website with our AI website builder on any paid plan.</p>



<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">You can use the AI assistant on any WordPress.com paid plan.</p>



<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">Sites on any paid plan can use MCP to connect to an AI agent.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-custom-domain" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">I already have a WordPress.com site. How do I start using AI tools?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">If you’re on a paid plan, go to your dashboard, enable the AI assistant, and it’ll appear inside your editor.</p>



<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">For MCP agent connections, head to <a href="https://wordpress.com/me/mcp/">your MCP settings</a> and follow the steps to connect your preferred agent. The whole setup takes a few minutes.</p>
</div>
</div></div></details>



<details data-event-name="faq-email-account" class="lp-block lp-question lp-record-click is-style-question-block-blueberry-5"><summary><div class="lp-question__summary"><div class="lp-question__summary__marker" aria-hidden="true"></div><div class="lp-question__summary__content">How much access does a connected AI agent have to my site?</div></div></summary><div class="lp-question__answer"><div class="lp-question__answer__content">
<div class="lp-block lp-content">
<p class="lp-gray-60 wp-block-paragraph">You control exactly what a connected agent can see. Access is scoped to what you authorize. You can review connected agents and revoke access at any time <a href="https://wordpress.com/me/mcp/">from your WordPress.com settings</a>.</p>

	.lp-floating-cursor {
		overflow: hidden;
		position: relative;
	}

	.lp-floating-cursor.lp-cursor-section .lp-section__content {
		position: static;
	}

	.lp-floating-cursor .lp-floating-cursor__target {
		position: absolute;
		transform: translate(calc(var(--lp-floating-cursor-left, 50%) - 50%), calc(var(--lp-floating-cursor-top, 50%) - 50%));
		pointer-events: none;
	}

	.lp-floating-cursor.lp-floating-cursor--background {
		background-position: var(--lp-floating-cursor-left, 50%) var(--lp-floating-cursor-top, 50%);
	}

	/* Decorative nebulae must never intercept clicks, wherever they sit on the page. */
	.lp-nebula {
		pointer-events: none;
	}

	.lp-floating-cursor .lp-floating-cursor__target > .lp-nebula {
		animation: lp-blur-pulse 6s infinite ease-in-out;
		filter: blur(calc(45px * var(--lp-nebula-blur-multiplier, 1)));
		pointer-events: none;
		transform: none;
		width: 100%;
	}

	/* Disable the blur animation in Safari for performance. */
	_::-webkit-full-page-media, _:future, :root .lp-floating-cursor .lp-floating-cursor__target > .lp-nebula {
		animation: none !important;
	}

	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
		.lp-floating-cursor .lp-floating-cursor__target > .lp-nebula {
			animation: none !important;
		}
	}

	@keyframes lp-blur-pulse {
		0%, 100% {
			filter: blur(calc(45px * var(--lp-nebula-blur-multiplier, 1)));
		}
		50% {
			filter: blur(calc(90px * var(--lp-nebula-blur-multiplier, 1)));
		}
	}

<script>
	document.addEventListener( 'DOMContentLoaded', () => {
		const cursors = document.querySelectorAll( '.lp-floating-cursor' );
		if ( ! cursors.length ) {
			return;
		}

		const motionQuery = window.matchMedia( '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' );
		const pointerQuery = window.matchMedia( '(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)' );
		const moveEvent = 'onpointermove' in window ? 'pointermove' : 'mousemove';
		const addQueryListener = ( query, listener ) => {
			if ( query.addEventListener ) {
				query.addEventListener( 'change', listener );
			} else {
				query.addListener( listener );
			}
		};

		cursors.forEach( cursor => {
			const target = cursor.querySelector( '.lp-floating-cursor__target' );
			const isBackground = cursor.classList.contains( 'lp-floating-cursor--background' );

			if ( ! target && ! isBackground ) {
				return;
			}

			if ( cursor.dataset.lpFloatingCursorInitialized === 'true' ) {
				return;
			}
			cursor.dataset.lpFloatingCursorInitialized = 'true';

			let animationFrame = null;
			const smoothingFactor = 0.05;
			const centerX = cursor.offsetWidth / 2;
			const centerY = cursor.offsetHeight / 2;
			let currentX = centerX;
			let currentY = centerY;
			let targetX = centerX;
			let targetY = centerY;

			cursor.style.setProperty( '--lp-floating-cursor-left', `${currentX}px` );
			cursor.style.setProperty( '--lp-floating-cursor-top', `${currentY}px` );

			const cancelAnimation = () => {
				if ( animationFrame !== null ) {
					cancelAnimationFrame( animationFrame );
					animationFrame = null;
				}
			};

			const canAnimate = () =>
				! motionQuery.matches &&
				pointerQuery.matches &&
				document.visibilityState === 'visible';

			const animateCursor = () => {
				animationFrame = null;

				if ( ! canAnimate() ) {
					return;
				}

				const dx = targetX - currentX;
				const dy = targetY - currentY;

				if ( Math.hypot( dx, dy ) < 0.1 ) {
					currentX = targetX;
					currentY = targetY;
					cursor.style.setProperty( '--lp-floating-cursor-left', `${currentX}px` );
					cursor.style.setProperty( '--lp-floating-cursor-top', `${currentY}px` );
					return;
				}

				currentX += dx * smoothingFactor;
				currentY += dy * smoothingFactor;

				cursor.style.setProperty( '--lp-floating-cursor-left', `${currentX}px` );
				cursor.style.setProperty( '--lp-floating-cursor-top', `${currentY}px` );
				animationFrame = requestAnimationFrame( animateCursor );
			};

			const startAnimation = () => {
				if ( animationFrame === null && canAnimate() ) {
					animationFrame = requestAnimationFrame( animateCursor );
				}
			};

			const handleStateChange = () => {
				if ( canAnimate() ) {
					startAnimation();
				} else {
					cancelAnimation();
				}
			};

			cursor.addEventListener( moveEvent, ( event ) => {
				if ( ! canAnimate() ) {
					cancelAnimation();
					return;
				}

				const rect = cursor.getBoundingClientRect();
				targetX = event.clientX - rect.left;
				targetY = event.clientY - rect.top;
				startAnimation();
			} );

			document.addEventListener( 'visibilitychange', handleStateChange );
			window.addEventListener( 'pagehide', cancelAnimation );
			window.addEventListener( 'pageshow', handleStateChange );
			addQueryListener( motionQuery, handleStateChange );
			addQueryListener( pointerQuery, handleStateChange );
		} );
	} );
</script>

<button type="button" class="wpcom-help-center-fab" aria-label="Help"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 24 24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path fill="currentColor" d="M11.07 12.85c.77-1.39 2.25-2.21 3.11-3.44.91-1.29.4-3.7-2.18-3.7-1.69 0-2.52 1.28-2.87 2.34L6.54 6.96C7.25 4.83 9.18 3 11.99 3c2.35 0 3.96 1.07 4.78 2.41.7 1.15 1.11 3.3.03 4.9-1.2 1.77-2.35 2.31-2.97 3.45-.25.46-.35.76-.35 2.24h-2.89c-.01-.78-.13-2.05.48-3.15zM14 20c0 1.1-.9 2-2 2s-2-.9-2-2 .9-2 2-2 2 .9 2 2z" /></svg><span class="screen-reader-text">Help</span></button>	<style id="wpcom-help-center-launcher-style">/* NOAUTORTL */
/* CSS logical properties handle direction at runtime; no RTL stylesheet needed. */
.wpcom-help-center-fab {
	position: fixed;
	inset-block-end: max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom));
	inset-inline-end: max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-right), env(safe-area-inset-left));
	width: 44px;
	height: 44px;
	padding: 0;
	border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 10%, transparent);
	border-radius: 50%;
	background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--studio-blue-50, #3858e9) 10%, var(--color-surface, #fff));
	color: var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d);
	font: inherit;
	cursor: pointer;
	display: inline-flex;
	align-items: center;
	justify-content: center;
	box-shadow:
		0 4px 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 1%, transparent),
		0 3px 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 2%, transparent),
		0 1px 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 2%, transparent),
		0 1px 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 3%, transparent);
	appearance: none;
	-webkit-appearance: none;
	opacity: 0;
	visibility: hidden;
	transition: background-color 0.15s ease-in-out, border-color 0.15s ease-in-out, opacity 0.2s ease;
	z-index: 200;
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab[data-hc-ready] {
	opacity: 1;
	visibility: visible;
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab:hover {
	background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--studio-blue-50, #3858e9) 16%, var(--color-surface, #fff));
	border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 14%, transparent);
	color: var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d);
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab[data-hc-open] {
	background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--studio-blue-50, #3858e9) 28%, var(--color-surface, #fff));
	border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 16%, transparent);
	color: var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d);
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab:focus {
	box-shadow:
		0 4px 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 1%, transparent),
		0 3px 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 2%, transparent),
		0 1px 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 2%, transparent),
		0 1px 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-neutral-100, #1d1d1d) 3%, transparent);
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab:focus:not(:focus-visible) {
	outline: none;
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab:focus-visible {
	outline: 2px solid var(--studio-blue-50, #3858e9);
	outline-offset: 2px;
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab svg {
	display: block;
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab--labeled {
	width: auto;
	height: 44px;
	padding: 0 16px;
	gap: 8px;
	border-radius: 22px;
}
/* Label-only while the label is visible; the icon returns when it hides (≤600px). */
.wpcom-help-center-fab--labeled svg {
	display: none;
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab__label {
	font-size: 14px;
	font-weight: 500;
	line-height: 1.2;
	white-space: nowrap;
}
/* Loading feedback for a pre-bootstrap click. */
.wpcom-help-center-fab[data-hc-loading] {
	cursor: progress;
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab[data-hc-loading] svg,
.wpcom-help-center-fab[data-hc-loading] .wpcom-help-center-fab__label {
	animation: wpcom-help-center-fab-pulse 1s ease-in-out infinite;
}
@keyframes wpcom-help-center-fab-pulse {
	50% {
		opacity: 0.35;
	}
}
.wpcom-help-center-fab .screen-reader-text {
	position: absolute;
	width: 1px;
	height: 1px;
	margin: -1px;
	padding: 0;
	overflow: hidden;
	clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
	border: 0;
	white-space: nowrap;
}
@media (max-width: 600px) {
	.wpcom-help-center-fab {
		inset-block-end: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom));
		inset-inline-end: max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-right), env(safe-area-inset-left));
	}
	/* Icon-only on small viewports; aria-label keeps the accessible name. */
	.wpcom-help-center-fab--labeled {
		width: 44px;
		padding: 0;
		border-radius: 50%;
	}
	.wpcom-help-center-fab--labeled svg {
		display: block;
	}
	.wpcom-help-center-fab__label {
		display: none;
	}
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
	.wpcom-help-center-fab {
		transition: none;
	}
	.wpcom-help-center-fab[data-hc-loading] svg,
	.wpcom-help-center-fab[data-hc-loading] .wpcom-help-center-fab__label {
		animation: none;
		opacity: 0.5;
	}
}

/* Anchor the desktop help-center modal so it clears our FAB (lift 8px
 * above the FAB top) and aligns with the FAB's trailing edge. `right: auto`
 * cancels the bundle's physical right:50px so the logical inset-inline-end
 * wins in RTL; !important outranks the CSS-in-JS rules wp-components
 * ships with the Card component. */
.help-center__container.is-desktop {
	bottom: calc(max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) + 52px) !important;
	right: auto !important;
	inset-inline-end: max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-right), env(safe-area-inset-left)) !important;
}

/* Clear the logged-out homepage's bottom-fixed "Code for the People" banner: 73px tall, 62px below 768px. */
body:has(.lp-cftp-banner) .wpcom-help-center-fab {
	inset-block-end: calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 89px);
}
body:has(.lp-cftp-banner) .help-center__container.is-desktop {
	bottom: calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 141px) !important;
}
@media (max-width: 767px) {
	body:has(.lp-cftp-banner) .wpcom-help-center-fab {
		inset-block-end: calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 78px);
	}
}

 * With cfg.immediate the FAB is revealed at script eval instead, only a click
 * bootstraps (no scroll, no timer), and a click before the bundle is ready shows [data-hc-loading]
 * and opens the Help Center when bootstrap completes within the watchdog
 * window; after a timeout the next click retries.

	const READY_ATTR = 'data-hc-ready';
	const OPEN_ATTR = 'data-hc-open';
	const LOADING_ATTR = 'data-hc-loading';
	const STORE_NAME = 'automattic/help-center';
	const TRACKS_SHOW_EVENT = 'wpcom_inlinehelp_show';
	const TRACKS_CLOSE_EVENT = 'wpcom_inlinehelp_close';
	const TRACKS_IMPRESSION_EVENT = 'wpcom_inlinehelp_impression';
	const TRACKS_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED_EVENT = 'wpcom_help_center_launcher_bootstrap_failed';
	const TRACKS_OPEN_PENDING_EVENT = 'wpcom_help_center_launcher_open_pending';

	}

			return Promise.resolve();

		if ( assetsLoad ) {
			return assetsLoad;
		}

		assetsLoad.catch( () => {
			assetsLoad = null;
		} );

	};

	const injectAssets = () => {
		const stylesheets = cfg.stylesheets || [];

		// Preload first so the actual injection below hits the browser cache.
		// Script injection stays serial to preserve WP print order around
		// inline before/data/after scripts.
		cfg.scripts.forEach( ( entry ) => {
			if ( entry.src ) {

						injectInline( entry.before );
						injectInline( entry.data );

							return entry.optional ? load.catch( () => {} ) : load;

		}
		const data = window.wp && window.wp.data;
		if ( ! data || ! data.subscribe || ! data.select ) {
			return;
		}
		const select = data.select( STORE_NAME );
		if ( ! select || ! select.isHelpCenterShown || ! fab ) {
			return;
		}
		storeSynced = true;
		let last;
		const update = () => {
			const shown = !! select.isHelpCenterShown();
			if ( shown === last ) {
				return;
			}
			last = shown;
			if ( shown ) {
				fab.setAttribute( OPEN_ATTR, '' );
			} else {

			}

	// no longer exist (stale ?ver). Re-fetch the entry bundle and stylesheets

			.filter( ( href ) => href.indexOf( '/help-center/' ) !== -1 )
			.forEach( ( href ) => appendLink( bust( href ), 'stylesheet' ) );
		const entry = cfg.scripts[ cfg.scripts.length - 1 ];
		await injectScript( bust( entry.src ) );

			await window.helpCenter.loadHelpCenter();
		}

		revealFab();
		openIfPending();

	// pulse forever either: at the timeout, stop the pulse and let the next
	// click retry; after three timeouts take the FAB down. A load that
	// finishes after a timeout still reveals the FAB — its side effects are
	// idempotent, so late success safely recovers.

		watchdog = null;
	};

		}

			if ( fab ) {
				fab.removeAttribute( LOADING_ATTR );

			if ( watchdogFires >= 3 ) {

			// worse than none. Record telemetry so we notice when the
			// upstream Help_Center contract drifts.
			trackBootstrapFailure( err );

			if ( immediate ) {
				clearWatchdog();
				pendingOpen = false;
				if ( fab ) {
					fab.removeAttribute( LOADING_ATTR );
					fab.removeAttribute( READY_ATTR );
				}
			}
		}
	};

	// Hoisted out of scheduleBootstrap so the immediate-mode click path can
	// trigger the same deduped start. `immediately` (user-initiated) skips
	// the idle wait.
	let started = false;
	const start = ( immediately ) => {
		if ( started ) {
			return;
		}
		started = true;
		// Needed when the fallback fired first; no-op when scroll won
		// (`once: true` already self-detached).
		window.removeEventListener( 'scroll', startOnScroll );
		if ( immediately ) {
			bootstrap();
			return;
		}
		if ( typeof window.requestIdleCallback === 'function' ) {
			window.requestIdleCallback( bootstrap, { timeout: 3000 } );
		} else {
			setTimeout( bootstrap, 0 );
		}
	};

	const startOnScroll = () => start();

	const scheduleBootstrap = () => {
		// Immediate mode bootstraps on FAB click only: no scroll trigger and no
		// post-load fallback, so nothing downloads unless the visitor asks.
		if ( immediate ) {
			return;
		}
		// Bootstrap on first scroll. The help-center bundle + its deps + CSS are
		// kilobytes of JS/CSS that we don't want in the initial-load budget —
		// Lighthouse audits don't scroll, so deferring here keeps the launcher
		// out of LCP/TBT/unused-JS metrics entirely. The FAB stays hidden
		// (data-hc-ready is set inside bootstrap) until the bundle is mounted.
		// Already-scrolled at script eval (hash navigation, back/forward scroll
		// restoration) — the scroll event won't fire, so kick off now.
		if ( window.scrollY > 0 ) {
			start();
			return;
		}
		window.addEventListener( 'scroll', startOnScroll, { once: true, passive: true } );
		// Safety net for short pages and above-the-fold lingerers — the
		// post-load delay sits outside the Lighthouse audit window.
		const scheduleFallback = () => setTimeout( start, BOOTSTRAP_FALLBACK_MS );

	// isn't available yet (e.g. bundle failed to load).

		const data = window.wp && window.wp.data;
		if ( ! data || ! data.dispatch || ! data.select ) {
			return null;
		}
		const dispatch = data.dispatch( STORE_NAME );
		const select = data.select( STORE_NAME );
		if ( ! dispatch || ! select || ! select.isHelpCenterShown ) {

		}

		// the target route; the app turns a bare route into a conversation resume.

					select.getHelpCenterRouterHistory && select.getHelpCenterRouterHistory();

				return !! top && top.pathname === route;
			} catch ( e ) {
				// Fall through to the navigate dispatch.
				return false;
			}
		};
		const willShow = ! select.isHelpCenterShown();
		if ( willShow ) {
			if ( ! immediate || ! routeAlreadyOnTop() ) {
				dispatch.setNavigateToRoute( route );
			}
			dispatch.showHelpCenter( true );
		} else {
			// Plain action, NOT the `setShowHelpCenter` thunk — that thunk
			// *returns* (instead of yielding) the visibility action, so a
			// fire-and-forget dispatch never updates state.
			dispatch.showHelpCenter( false );
		}
		return willShow;
	};

	// Immediate mode: a click arrived before the store existed; open once
	// bootstrap lands and clear the loading state.
	const openIfPending = () => {
		if ( ! pendingOpen ) {
			return;
		}
		pendingOpen = false;
		clearWatchdog();
		if ( fab ) {
			fab.removeAttribute( LOADING_ATTR );
		}
		// Already shown (the app restores persisted open state) — toggling
		// would close it.
		const data = window.wp && window.wp.data;
		const select = data && data.select && data.select( STORE_NAME );
		if ( select && select.isHelpCenterShown && select.isHelpCenterShown() ) {
			return;
		}
		const willShow = toggleHelpCenter();
		if ( willShow ) {
			track( TRACKS_SHOW_EVENT, { location: 'fab', section: section() } );
		} else if ( null === willShow ) {
			// Bootstrap resolved without the store; let the next click retry.
			started = false;
			trackBootstrapFailure( 'store-missing' );
		}
	};

	const handleClick = ( clickEvent ) => {
		if ( ! clickEvent.target.closest( SELECTOR ) ) {
			return;
		}
		clickEvent.preventDefault();
		const willShow = toggleHelpCenter();
		if ( willShow !== null ) {
			track( willShow ? TRACKS_SHOW_EVENT : TRACKS_CLOSE_EVENT, { location: 'fab', section: section() } );
			return;
		}
		if ( immediate ) {
			// Pending opens vs. eventual shows make spinner abandonment
			// measurable; once per loading episode, not per click.
			if ( ! pendingOpen ) {
				track( TRACKS_OPEN_PENDING_EVENT, { location: 'fab', section: section() } );
			}
			pendingOpen = true;
			if ( fab ) {
				fab.setAttribute( LOADING_ATTR, '' );
			}
			startWatchdog();
			start( true );
		}
	};

	document.addEventListener( 'click', handleClick );
} )();

document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
    const API_GEO_ENDPOINT = 'https://public-api.wordpress.com/geo/';
    const FCCA_LINK_SELECTOR = '.lp-footer-stack [data-is-fcca]';

    function fetchGeoData() {
        return fetch( API_GEO_ENDPOINT ).then( res => res.json() );
    }

    function removeLink( selector, condition ) {
        document.querySelectorAll( selector ).forEach( element => {
            const parent = element.parentNode;
            const parentTagName = parent.tagName.toLowerCase();

            if ( condition ) {
                (parentTagName === 'li' ? parent : element).remove();
            }
        });
    }

    /**
     * Checks if the given data pertains to the specified region or country
     * @param {string} key - The key to check in the data
     * @param {string} name - The region or country name to check for
     * @param {object} data - The geolocation data
     * @returns {boolean} - True if the data pertains to the specified region or country
     */
    function pertainsTo( key, name, data ) {
        if ( data && data[ key ] && name ) {
            return data[ key ].toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase();
        }

        return false;
    }

    fetchGeoData().then(data => {
        const isFCCA = pertainsTo( 'country_long', 'germany', data );
        removeLink( FCCA_LINK_SELECTOR, ! isFCCA );
    });
});

Try the AI website builder AI, meet WordPress WordPress AI brings helpful support to building and managing your site — from getting started to creating content to connecting your site to trusted AI agents and beyond. WordPress Agent WordPress Agent works alongside you inside the editor to write content, refine layouts, adjust design, and navigate WordPress, with image generation and editing also built into the Media Library. Enable WordPress Agent Write with confidence Get suggestions that sharpen your message, improve clarity, and help your content connect without losing your voice or breaking your flow. Shape as you go Make context-aware design updates, adjust layouts, and refine your visual identity right in the editor — no switching tools or starting from scratch. Visuals, your way Generate original images, edit existing ones, and refine visuals to fit your brand without leaving your site or opening another app. MCP Enable AI agents like Claude and ChatGPT to read, write, and manage your WordPress.com site — content, comments, media, and more — through natural conversation, without ever opening your dashboard. Enable MCP Your workflow Connect your favorite AI agent to your site and manage content, check performance, and stay organized without opening the dashboard. Gets your style Your AI agent reads your theme, colors, fonts, and structure first, so anything it creates actually fits your site, not a generic template. You’re in control Nothing changes on your site without your say-so. You choose what AI can do, site by site, and confirm every update before it happens. AI website builder Chat to generate a full WordPress site you can continue to customize as you grow. No fragile, one-off code to manage. Just a fast and secure site built on the world’s most popular website builder. Try the AI website builder Skip the blank screen Describe what you need, and go from idea to a complete WordPress site in minutes — no design skills, no code, no staring at an empty page. Uniquely yours Your site is built on your input, not a rigid template. Adjust text, images, colors, and layout until it feels like you, then publish when you’re ready. WordPress from the start Your site launches on WordPress.com with managed hosting, security, and support built in so you can keep building without outgrowing the platform. WordPress Agent on Telegram Your WordPress site, always in reach. Chat with the agent on Telegram so you can publish, update, and manage from your phone — no dashboard, no setup, just a conversation. Scan the QR code or click the link below to start. Message WordPress Agent Just show up No plugins to install, no tools to configure, no learning curve. Connect your WordPress.com account once and you’re ready to go. On-the-go Good ideas and urgent fixes don’t wait until you’re at a desk. Publish a post on your commute, check your traffic from a coffee shop, fix a typo mid-meeting — no laptop needed. Studio Code Studio Code is an AI agent that builds complete WordPress sites from a prompt. Run it from your terminal or the WordPress Studio desktop app, tell it what you want — a portfolio, a storefront, a landing page — and it handles the theme, content, plugins, and design, checking its own work until the result looks right. Now in beta. Learn more about Studio Code Vibe code your WordPress Describe the site you want in natural language, and Studio Code gets it done. Built with AI, loved by users AI did most of the work in 5 minutes, where it would’ve taken me 2 days, including watching a bunch of ‘how to’ videos. Zander Lourens , Owner & music producer for Gratia dei Studio Loved how easy it was to insert pictures and change things. Steve C. , Steve’s car care It leveraged very nice assets and gave us a canvas to iterate and tune with minimal effort/time. Don G. , Manager I liked how he responded to get more info from me. It was like having a partner with someone who has my best interest. Kerry L. , Coach It was a dream come true. Nicole G. , Small business owner WordPress AI FAQ Try the AI website builder Does WordPress AI replace my creativity or writing? No. WordPress AI is designed to support your work, not replace it, so you stay in control of ideas, voice, and decisions. AI helps with things like tightening copy, improving clarity, formatting layouts, and optimizing for SEO when you ask. Can I use WordPress AI just as an editor? Yes. Many creators use the AI assistant to refine existing, human-written text — making it clearer, more concise, or better structured — without having AI generate content from scratch. Is WordPress AI only for building new sites? No. The AI website builder helps you create a site from scratch, and the AI assistant supports ongoing updates and improvements inside your existing site. What can the AI assistant actually help me with? Quite a lot. Inside your editor, you can ask it to rewrite or refine text, adjust tone, translate content, generate images from a description, edit existing photos in your Media Library, modify block styles and color palettes, create new pages, and navigate WordPress using plain language. You can also chain multiple requests together and it’ll handle them in sequence. Does the AI assistant know what’s on my site, or only general information? The AI assistant has context about the content you’re actively working on in the editor, but it doesn’t crawl or index your entire site by default. For deeper, site-wide awareness — like analyzing your content strategy or comparing pages — that’s what MCP agent connections are for. Can the AI assistant translate my content into other languages? Yes. You can ask the assistant to translate any text block into another language directly within the editor. It works across posts, pages, and other editable content on your site. What’s the difference between the AI assistant and a connected AI agent? The AI assistant is your in-editor helper — it responds to requests as you work and helps you create and edit content in real time. A connected AI agent (via MCP) is an external AI tool, like Claude, that you give read access to your site so it can analyze your content and provide deeper, data-driven insights. Think of the assistant as your writing partner and agents as your analysts. Which plans include WordPress AI? Build a website with our AI website builder on any paid plan. You can use the AI assistant on any WordPress.com paid plan. Sites on any paid plan can use MCP to connect to an AI agent. I already have a WordPress.com site. How do I start using AI tools? If you’re on a paid plan, go to your dashboard, enable the AI assistant, and it’ll appear inside your editor. For MCP agent connections, head to your MCP settings and follow the steps to connect your preferred agent. The whole setup takes a few minutes. How much access does a connected AI agent have to my site? You control exactly what a connected agent can see. Access is scoped to what you authorize. You can review connected agents and revoke access at any time from your WordPress.com settings . Which AI agents can I connect to my WordPress.com site? WordPress.com has an official Claude (Anthropic) connector . Any AI tool that supports MCP — the open standard for AI agent connectivity — can also be connected. Can I use WordPress-related Agent Skills while building my project? Yes. Agent Skills are a curated set of reusable “skills” (prompt/tooling packages) you can add to an AI agent’s toolbox to help it work more effectively on WordPress-related development tasks. Learn more about using and installing WordPress Agent Skills in our documentation . Your dream site, live in minutes Prompt, edit, and launch WordPress websites with AI. mainEntity.name: Does WordPress AI replace my creativity or writing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. WordPress AI is designed to support your work, not replace it, so you stay in control of ideas, voice, and decisions. AI helps with things like tightening copy, improving clarity, formatting layouts, and optimizing for SEO when you ask.

mainEntity.name: Can I use WordPress AI just as an editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many creators use the AI assistant to refine existing, human-written text — making it clearer, more concise, or better structured — without having AI generate content from scratch.

mainEntity.name: Is WordPress AI only for building new sites?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The AI website builder helps you create a site from scratch, and the AI assistant supports ongoing updates and improvements inside your existing site.

mainEntity.name: What can the AI assistant actually help me with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quite a lot. Inside your editor, you can ask it to rewrite or refine text, adjust tone, translate content, generate images from a description, edit existing photos in your Media Library, modify block styles and color palettes, create new pages, and navigate WordPress using plain language. You can also chain multiple requests together and it’ll handle them in sequence.

mainEntity.name: Does the AI assistant know what’s on my site, or only general information?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AI assistant has context about the content you’re actively working on in the editor, but it doesn’t crawl or index your entire site by default. For deeper, site-wide awareness — like analyzing your content strategy or comparing pages — that’s what MCP agent connections are for.

mainEntity.name: Can the AI assistant translate my content into other languages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can ask the assistant to translate any text block into another language directly within the editor. It works across posts, pages, and other editable content on your site.

mainEntity.name: What’s the difference between the AI assistant and a connected AI agent?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AI assistant is your in-editor helper — it responds to requests as you work and helps you create and edit content in real time. A connected AI agent (via MCP) is an external AI tool, like Claude, that you give read access to your site so it can analyze your content and provide deeper, data-driven insights. Think of the assistant as your writing partner and agents as your analysts.

mainEntity.name: Which plans include WordPress AI?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Build a website with our AI website builder on any paid plan.

You can use the AI assistant on any WordPress.com paid plan.

Sites on any paid plan can use MCP to connect to an AI agent.

mainEntity.name: I already have a WordPress.com site. How do I start using AI tools?

acceptedAnswer.text:
If you’re on a paid plan, go to your dashboard, enable the AI assistant, and it’ll appear inside your editor.

For MCP agent connections, head to your MCP settings and follow the steps to connect your preferred agent. The whole setup takes a few minutes.

mainEntity.name: How much access does a connected AI agent have to my site?

acceptedAnswer.text: You control exactly what a connected agent can see. Access is scoped to what you authorize. You can review connected agents and revoke access at any time from your WordPress.com settings.

mainEntity.name: Which AI agents can I connect to my WordPress.com site?

acceptedAnswer.text: WordPress.com has an official Claude (Anthropic) connector. Any AI tool that supports MCP — the open standard for AI agent connectivity — can also be connected.

mainEntity.name: Can I use WordPress-related Agent Skills while building my project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Agent Skills are a curated set of reusable “skills” (prompt/tooling packages) you can add to an AI agent’s toolbox to help it work more effectively on WordPress-related development tasks. Learn more about using and installing WordPress Agent Skills in our documentation.

<script id="landpack-nav-script-js-after">
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
    const API_GEO_ENDPOINT = 'https://public-api.wordpress.com/geo/';
    const FCCA_LINK_SELECTOR = '.lp-footer-stack [data-is-fcca]';

    function fetchGeoData() {
        return fetch( API_GEO_ENDPOINT ).then( res => res.json() );
    }

    function removeLink( selector, condition ) {
        document.querySelectorAll( selector ).forEach( element => {
            const parent = element.parentNode;
            const parentTagName = parent.tagName.toLowerCase();

            if ( condition ) {
                (parentTagName === 'li' ? parent : element).remove();
            }
        });
    }

    /**
     * Checks if the given data pertains to the specified region or country
     * @param {string} key - The key to check in the data
     * @param {string} name - The region or country name to check for
     * @param {object} data - The geolocation data
     * @returns {boolean} - True if the data pertains to the specified region or country
     */
    function pertainsTo( key, name, data ) {
        if ( data && data[ key ] && name ) {
            return data[ key ].toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase();
        }

        return false;
    }

    fetchGeoData().then(data => {
        const isFCCA = pertainsTo( 'country_long', 'germany', data );
        removeLink( FCCA_LINK_SELECTOR, ! isFCCA );
    });
});
//# sourceURL=landpack-nav-script-js-after
</script>

	document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
		const API_GEO_ENDPOINT = 'https://public-api.wordpress.com/geo/';
		const FCCA_LINK_SELECTOR = '.lp-footer-stack [data-is-fcca]';

		function fetchGeoData() {
			return fetch(API_GEO_ENDPOINT).then(res => res.json());

		function removeLink(selector, condition) {
			document.querySelectorAll(selector).forEach(element => {
				const parent = element.parentNode;
				const parentTagName = parent.tagName.toLowerCase();

				if (condition) {
					(parentTagName === 'li' ? parent : element).remove();
				}
			});
		}
		
		/**
		 * Checks if the given data pertains to the specified region or country
		 * @param {string} key - The key to check in the data
		 * @param {string} name - The region or country name to check for
		 * @param {object} data - The geolocation data
		 * @returns {boolean} - True if the data pertains to the specified region or country
		 */
		function pertainsTo(key, name, data) {
			if (data && data[key] && name) {
				return data[key].toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase();
			}

			return false;
		}

		fetchGeoData().then(data => {
			const isFCCA = pertainsTo('country_long', 'germany', data);
			removeLink(FCCA_LINK_SELECTOR, !isFCCA);
